findings.text: Provides node scoped initialization for generational LRU bookkeeping of memory control groups, preparing its lock and generation bin lists for later use.
Provides allocation of the per node descriptor for a node identifier that lacks one, used when bringing offline or memoryless nodes into the initialization path.
Offers on demand initialization of deferred tail pages for the final zone of a node when early allocation pressure requires more initialized pages.
Exposes marking of one pageblock as contiguous allocation area with corresponding managed and zone accounting updates.

Covers late phase responsibilities including completion of deferred initialization, stable accounting reporting, early allocator discard, free page shuffling, contiguity detection, extension setup and control registration.
Entry for randomizing free page order across every zone of a node once shuffling is enabled.
Public initialization of per page extension storage across memory nodes with notifier registration and callback invocation.
Registers virtual memory allocator controls under the virtual memory control hierarchy.

Pageblock granularity is established at most once; an already set order is preserved, otherwise a compile time maximum is capped by huge page granularity when huge pages are finer. An alternate build provides no operation.

Flag storage for pageblocks is absent for empty zones and otherwise sized to cover the aligned span with per block bits rounded to machine word granularity. Failure to obtain node local storage is fatal. An alternate build leaves the pointer unset and performs no work.

After per node internal setup, each zone descriptor is internally initialized with managed pages starting from zero; empty zones stop there while populated zones also receive flag storage and empty zone state.

The node page descriptor array covers a buddy aligned interval enclosing the node range with an offset adjusted base; the global map aliases the first node with matching correction and the maximum map number reflects the aligned span. Empty nodes are skipped and an alternate build does nothing.

Node initialization records identity and physical range, distinguishes populated from memoryless nodes for total page accounting, then ensures descriptor array, deferred range, core zone setup and generational LRU setup are all established.

Deferred page descriptors are initialized over a caller supplied interval within one zone. Release of deferred ranges treats empty input as success, treats a fully aligned maximum order span as one large block, and otherwise accepts smaller spans before releasing single pages, with movable migration marking applied upfront.

Deferred work over an interval is restricted to free physical ranges clipped to that interval and split at maximum order alignment, with cooperative scheduling behavior selected by caller context. Thread fan out for a node is at least one and scales with node processor count.

Per node deferred initialization claims the pending start marker under resize protection, validates it against node bounds, marks further growth closed, processes only the highest zone up to section alignment with section sized parallel chunks, then reports completion.

Extension storage need and per operation offsets are derived from registered operations in two passes, with shared flag demand forcing a base record size. Section tables are allocated once, biased so section start indexes correctly, and total consumption is tracked. Allocation prefers node exact zeroed pages with virtual fallback and page accounting.
Shuffling is globally gated by a runtime key and otherwise walks all zones of a node; an alternate build never shuffles.

Zone limit ordering direction depends on a specific architecture configuration. High memory pointer preserves an early architecture value and otherwise derives from end of dynamic RAM capped for high memory layouts. Node capability flags for high and normal memory are set from the lowest populated ordinary zone.

Boot memory summary adjusts kernel section sizes for embedding and overlap cases before reporting available, kernel code, data, rodata, init, bss, reserved, contiguous reserved and optionally high memory totals.
Resize protection serializes access to the pending deferred start marker between background initialization and on demand growth, preventing concurrent claims and lost updates.
Generational LRU initialization prepares its spin lock before any bin use; no acquisition occurs during setup itself.

Zone and node descriptors exchange start frame, spanned and present counts, flag storage, descriptor base, deferred marker, zone count and highest reclaimer index during bring up, with per processor node statistics pointed at early boot storage.
Section extension pointer stores a biased base that compensates for section start so that frame indexed access lands in the allocated table; a non null value means the section is already initialized.
Parallel deferred work is described by a job record carrying function, zone argument, start, size, section alignment, minimum chunk, thread limit and locality policy.

Boot allocator bring up moves from architecture limits through movable range discovery, diagnostic dumps, page flag validation, node count and pageblock setup, per node initialization with memory state marking, kernel page counting, hash distribution fixup and high memory finalization.

Deferred initialization moves from per memory node thread launch through parallel section processing and on demand growth to completion barrier, permanent disable of on demand path, and limit reinitialization.
Node memory presence moves from range discovery to populated versus memoryless accounting, then to memory capability marking only when present pages exist.
Page extension bring up moves from need detection through per section allocation and notifier registration to init callback invocation, aborting the boot on allocation failure.
Main boot time entry that establishes zone ranges and node descriptors before the allocator serves general requests.
Late boot entry invoked after general kernel bring up to finish deferred page work and publish allocator state.
Per node thread entry that performs background initialization of the deferred tail of the highest zone.
Late entry that provisions extension tables after all page descriptors are initialized, conditional on deferred descriptor mode.
Exhaustion of early node storage for flag maps, descriptor arrays or extension tables aborts boot rather than continuing with incomplete metadata.

Inconsistent deferred bounds, unexpected population of the zone after the highest one, mismatched node data expectations, non zero node state at entry and illegal growth targets are treated as programming errors with traps or warnings.

Overlapping node frame ranges, unaligned node boundaries and non section aligned deferred tails require filtering by validity, ownership and alignment to avoid double initialization or use of uninitialized descriptors.
Adaptive scaling uses a sixty four gibibyte base with a shift of two; the page count form is the base expressed in pages.
